column4: why

Concentration in equilibrium with 35 Pa CO2 in the GAS PHASE at 35 C, organism Generic. An extracellular equilibrium, not an E. coli intracellular pool -- a respiring cell makes its own CO2 and sits far above air equilibrium.

Solubility of CO2 in water at 25 C and 1 atm partial pressure, organism Generic. A solubility table needs a partial pressure assumption to become a concentration, which makes it a derivation rather than a measurement.
Solubility of CO2 in water at 35 C and 1 atm partial pressure. Same defect as 106207.
Solubility of CO2 in water at 15 C, in grams per 100 ml. Same defect, and not at growth temperature.
Standard redox potential of water/oxygen, 800 mV. A midpoint potential is a standard quantity eQuilibrator's dG' already accounts for, not an in-vivo poise.
Redox potential for the carbohydrate unit. Same defect as 104500.
Diffusion coefficient of oxygen in water. A transport property, not a concentration.
Diffusion coefficient of oxygen in water. Same as 100615.
Diffusion coefficient of oxygen in water. Same as 100615.
The oxygen concentration at which respiration still makes ~50% of normal pmf. A threshold in an experiment, not a physiological pool.
The oxygen concentration at which respiration still makes near-maximal pmf. Same defect as 111065.
Growth rate on gluconate at high oxygen. A rate in hour^-1, not a concentration.
Growth rate on gluconate at low oxygen. Same as 106799.
NAD+/NADH ratio from Henry 2006, which is a THERMODYNAMIC FIT. Feeding a thermodynamically-derived number back into a thermodynamic calculation is circular.
NADP+/NADPH ratio from Henry 2006. Same defect as 105022.
